1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of the average recent 7-day mean.

2. Forecasts tend to lag behind true values by 1–3 days — apply a 1-day forward shift in the forecast curve to align with observed momentum.

3. After sharp price spikes (e.g., >3% from prior day), model overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the immediate prior day’s true value.

4. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if true price deviates >2.5σ from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward the moving average with a 0.7x decay factor.

5. Forecasts for the first 5 days of the 30-day window are systematically too low — apply a 1.2x multiplier to the first 5 forecasted values to compensate for initial lag.

6. Model fails to capture late-period volatility — increase forecast variance in final 5 days by 15–20% if true outcome shows >1.5σ deviation from prior 10-day average.
